data.title: Railway PSU stocks derailed! RVNL, IRFC, IRCON, RITES to IRCTC down 60% in yr- What went wrong? Experts explain
data.description:
Railway PSU stocks, Oct. 17 -- Top railway public sector undertaking stocks, including Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, Indian Railways Finance Corporation (IRFC), IRCON International, RITES, to Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), have seen a sharp decline of up to 40% over the past year.

The steep correction has left investors wondering what went wrong and whether the worst is over. Let's understand from experts, along with their take on railway PSU stocks outlook.

The decline in railway PSU stocks is more of a correction after decades of rally, according to Tushar Badjate, Director of Badjate Stock & shares Pvt Ltd.

"This is a valuation correction first and an earnings correction second. In 2023 and 2024, these stocks were priced for a decade of perfection. IRCTC hit an all-time high of Rs.1,318 in May 2024 and is now down about 61% from that peak. RVNL and IRFC have fallen between 45% and 53% from their 52-week highs," added Badjate while highlighting that three things went wrong for these PSU stocks.

Slow growth and decline in margins were among the key things that went wrong for railway PSUs. "What did not break is spending. Railway capex for FY27 is a record Rs.2.93 lakh crore. The money is flowing. It is just not reaching these companies at the old margins," highlighted Badjate.

PSU stocks often attract heightened investor interest because of their government-backing, relative stability and long-term growth prospects. The sharp correction in railway PSU stocks is largely a result of investor expectations running ahead of fundamentals, according to Tushar Badjate.

However earnings concerns are real and they are about margins not orders, underlined the expert.

"Order books look healthy. RVNL has Rs.93,492 crore and RITES has a record Rs.9,445 crore. The problem is conversion. Only about Rs.40,000 crore of RVNL's book is actually under execution. Its EBITDA margin is just 4.4%. IRCTC grew revenue 18% last quarter, yet profit was flat as its margin fell to 28.2% from 34.3%. IRCON's consolidated profit dropped to Rs.92.7 crore from Rs.164.6 crore on losses from joint ventures. These companies are no longer protected monopolies. They are contractors competing for work. Contractors do not deserve 50 to 60 times earnings," he added.

The correction has improved valuations for some railway PSU stocks not for all of them in the segment, noted Badjate calling IRFC a safer choice for conservative, income-focused investors.

Over the next 12 months, Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza, expects railway PSUs to ride a sustained capex cycle with Indian Railways' FY27 capital outlay at a record Rs.2.93 lakh crore.

"RVNL offers the deepest visibility with a Rs. 93,492 crore order book, guidance of about 15% revenue growth and diversification into ports, hydro and overseas work, though thin margins cap upside," explained Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza.

IRFC stock's primary trend remains bearish as the ongoing momentum hints at series of lower highs and lower lows from its peak. "Although the RSI at 52.56 indicates a slight neutral recovery attempt, it lacks decisive momentum. This is not a fresh buying opportunity because the stock remains trapped under a heavy bearish structure," stated Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza.

Downtrend defined by continuous sliding from above 720 to its current level highlights IRCTC's outlook.

"All key moving averages are aligned in a downward bearish stack-20 EMA (463.97), 50 EMA (474.05), 100 EMA (494.56), and 200 EMA (539.51)-with price consolidating right around the 20 EMA," highlighted Jagad, while adding caution that it is not a fresh buying opportunity as buying into an ongoing, structurally weak downtrend carries high risk.

Akin to other peers in the category, RVNL also remains locked in a persistent downward trend. The stock is hovering close to its 20 EMA, while it remained firmly suppressed underneath its 50 EMA, 100 EMA and 200 EMA.

"An RSI reading of 47.05 reflects weak neutral momentum with no strong bullish divergence present on the daily chart. This is not a fresh buying opportunity because current price action merely represents a minor relief bounce within a broader drop," noted Virat Jagad.

RailTel is displaying a strong long-term bearish bias as it declines from above 380 to current levels around 255.40. "The RSI at 45.60 sits below the neutral 50 threshold, highlighting persistent underlying weakness. This is not a fresh buying opportunity due to heavy overhead supply across multiple moving average barriers," Jagad added.

data.title: Portable mini speakers compared: 5 picks for battery life, sound and easy carrying
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- No outdoors getaway or party is complete without the right set of tracks setting the mood. Sure you can play songs on your smartphone, but that is often not enough especially when you are out with a group of friends or family members.

This is where a compact Bluetooth speaker becomes important. The right speaker that is somewhat light in weight, is easy to carry, last long enough between charges and sound good for its size is what you need to on road trips or at picnics. That said, buying the smallest or cheapest model does not always guarantee a satisfying listening experience. Some compact speakers prioritise portability over battery life, while others offer longer playback but take up more space in your bag.

Before choosing one, look at three essentials: battery backup, sound quality and portability. A longer-lasting battery means fewer charging breaks during travel, while clear vocals and balanced bass can make music and podcasts more enjoyable. Weight, water resistance and build quality also matter if you plan to use your speaker outdoors or carry it around regularly.

To help you find the right fit, we have compared five portable mini speakers across these key factors. This list explores what each model offers, from pocket-friendly designs to options built for longer listening sessions. Whether you are shopping on a tight budget or willing to spend more for better features, this guide will help you find the right model for your needs.

The JBL Go 4 is a compact Bluetooth speaker designed for music on the go, with a lightweight build that easily fits into a bag or pocket. Its IP67 rating provides protection against dust and water, which makes it suitable for outdoor adventures, poolside listening and travel. The rugged design adds everyday practicality, while Bluetooth connectivity enables wireless music playback from compatible devices. A USB Type-C port handles charging, and the built-in battery offers up to seven hours of playback.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality amazing and appreciate its portability, being easy to carry outdoors and perfect for travel, with one customer noting it fits in the palm of their hand. They praise its compact size, appearance, and seamless Bluetooth connectivity, and consider it good value for money.

Buyers should choose this Bluetooth speaker for its sound quality, connectivity and design.

The Sony ULT Field 1 is a rugged portable Bluetooth speaker built for listeners who want punchy bass and dependable battery life. Its dedicated ULT button boosts low frequencies, giving music a deeper, more energetic sound, while Sony's Sound Diffusion Processor helps deliver a more expansive listening experience. The compact speaker features a detachable strap for easy carrying and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. Its battery promises up to 12 hours of playback.

Buyers praise the speaker's sound quality, describing it as ultra clear and balanced, while also appreciating its build quality and compact size. The battery life is impressive. They find it easy to carry and use, making it ideal for home and work outdoor use.

Buyers should choose this sound quality, battery life and connectivity.

The boAt Stone 1200 Pro is a portable Bluetooth speaker built for listeners who want powerful sound and bass-heavy music. Its 60W output, two 2.75-inch full-range drivers and dual radiators aim to deliver punchy bass and clear highs for parties and outdoor gatherings. The rugged, elongated design includes a carry strap for easier transport and an IPX6 rating for protection against water splashes. Battery life reaches up to 7.5 hours at 50% volume, while True Wireless Stereo pairing lets you connect two compatible speakers for a bigger soundstage.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality amazing and appreciate its impressive battery backup, with one mentioning it can run for 6-7 hours on 50% charge. The build quality is excellent, and they consider it worth the price point.

Buyers should choose this sound quality and battery life.

The JBL Charge 6 combines a rugged, portable design with powerful JBL Pro Sound, delivering rich bass and crisp highs for music at home or outdoors. Its AI Sound Boost technology analyses audio in real time to improve output while reducing distortion. The removable handle strap makes carrying easier, while IP68 protection guards against dust and water. Battery life reaches up to 24 hours, with Playtime Boost adding four more hours.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality excellent, particularly praising its crisp clear vocals and bass performance. They appreciate its appearance and consider it well worth the money.

Buyers should choose this sound quality and design.

The Xiaomi Sound Outdoor 30W features a compact, cylindrical design with an anti-slip lanyard, making it convenient for travel, picnics and outdoor gatherings. Its 30W audio system combines a 20W woofer, 10W tweeter and dual passive radiators for punchy bass and clear highs. The IP67-rated body resists dust and water, while Bluetooth 5.4 enables wireless streaming. Its 2,600mAh battery promises up to 12 hours of playback at 50% volume, and USB-C charging takes approximately 2.5 hours.

Buyers praise the speaker's sound quality, with one noting it fills a 200 square feet room at 40% volume, and its 12-hour battery life at 50% volume. Moreover, the build quality is excellent.

Buyers should choose this sound quality, battery life and design.

data.title: Bitcoin Bounces Off Its Lowest Point In A Month, But Charles Schwab’s Adam Lynch Warns A Midterms Risk
data.description:
Key points:
  • Charles Schwab’s Adam Lynch said crypto’s progress in Washington could “grind to a halt” if the midterm elections change who holds power.
  • However, he remained “somewhat optimistic” about a bipartisan deal.
  • Bitcoin rebounded after dipping to around $80,000, its lowest level since Sept. 18. Lynch said leverage has made the recent swings sharper.

Bitcoin (BTC) rebounded from its lowest point in nearly a month on Saturday, but Charles Schwab’s (SCHW) Adam Lynch warned that midterms could “grind [crypto industry] to a halt”.

Lynch, Director of Equity Research at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, made the comments in an interview with Schwab Network. He called the current administration “probably the most pro-crypto and crypto-friendly” one so far.

On Friday, Charles Schwab rolled out direct Bitcoin purchases to all eligible retail clients among its 40 million clients.

Bitcoin Rebounds From Monthly Low 

BTC dipped to around $80,000 on Thursday, its lowest level since September 18. It has since rebounded since then. Lynch said leverage made the recent swings sharper. Traders who piled into long bets near $87,000 earlier this month were wiped out, he said, and the rebound also forced out some short sellers.

Bitcoin's price was trading at $81,545, down by 0.6% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day. According to platform data, watchers for the apex cryptocurrency dropped nearly 47% over the past 30 days.

Ethereum Lags, But Bitcoin’s Fundamentals Hold

According to Lynch, Ethereum (ETH) has had it worse. He said it “hit a little bit harder this month,” while Bitcoin had “been the better performer.” Ethereum is down about 18% so far this year, compared to Bitcoin’s 7% decline.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Ethereum remained in the extremely bearish zone, accompanied by low chatter levels over the past day. According to platform data, watchers for Ethereum dropped nearly 36% over the past 30 days.

But Lynch said Bitcoin’s long-term fundamentals have not changed. He noted that US Bitcoin exchange-traded products have brought in nearly $60 billion since January 2024. “It’s become a major player,” he said.

Why The Midterms Matter For Crypto

Lynch’s comments came as crypto legislation has been stuck in Congress after the market structure bill failed to pass. Regulators, however, were making progress on their own, he pointed out, talking about a “rulemaking process” the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) started “about 10 days ago” to build a “tailored framework for certain crypto transactions.” He said the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) was also working on a broader digital asset framework.

“From the regulatory standpoint, I think we will see progress, and that will hopefully help the market,” he said.

That regulatory progress has come under an administration Lynch called the most crypto-friendly yet, which is why he sees the midterms as a risk.

President Donald Trump has pledged to make the US the “crypto capital of the world,” and has vowed the country will dominate the sector. He signed an executive order creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and, last year, signed the GENIUS Act, the first federal law for stablecoins.

Opposition Adds Uncertainty Ahead Of Midterms

However, not everyone in Washington shared that view. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), one of crypto’s most vocal critics, pressed the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) in May over trust charters granted to crypto firms, including Ripple (XRP), Coinbase (COIN) and Paxos (USDP). She had also urged the Fed and Treasury not to use taxpayer money to rescue crypto investors.

A power shift could give crypto critics like Warren more say over that agenda. Lynch, however, still hoped for a deal. He said lawmakers have tried hard to find common ground on crypto. “So I’m still somewhat optimistic.”

data.title: Silver's recent 50% drop from a record high hints that an economic slowdown looms
data.description:
By Myra P. Saefong

Silver is more 'economically sensitive' than gold, notes one precious-metals dealer

Silver's price action may offer hints on the economy amid inflation driven by rising fuel prices.

There's a relatively off-the-radar commodity that can provide hints on where the economy is headed - and it's seen its value drop more than 50% from a record high earlier this year.

"Silver is more economically sensitive than gold, so its recent price weakness may be a leading indicator of underlying issues in the broader economy," said Stefan Gleason, president and CEO at Money Metals Exchange.

Silver can be seen as hybrid leading indicator because of its dual role as a monetary precious metal and an industrial commodity. Prices for silver (SIZ26) (SI00) reached a record intraday high of $121.79 an ounce in late January, according to Dow Jones Market Data - but have since dropped more than 50% to end at $57.31 an ounce Friday.

Gold (GCZ26) (GC00) has dropped too, but nowhere near as much as silver. The yellow metal has lost over 25% from its record high of $5,626.80 an ounce in January.

Silver's decline "syncs up with the warning lights we are seeing in the energy markets - with persistently high energy prices virtually certain to slow the economy, or worse," Gleason told MarketWatch.

Year to date, U.S. and global benchmark prices for crude oil (CL.1) (BRN00) have climbed by more than 70%, in large part due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East that has disrupted production and shipments of the commodity. In a sign of the rising cost of refined oil, the price of diesel at the pump has spiked nearly 78% since the end of last year to stand at $6.30 a gallon Friday, according to GasBuddy.

Those increases were evident in the latest U.S. inflation data, which showed hotter prices than the market expected. The consumer-price index rose 0.6% in September and gained 3.7% year over year, while the producer-price index was up 1.3% last month and climbed 6.3% year over year.

Silver, meanwhile, is "reflecting some of the economic headwinds higher inflation is causing in the global economy," said Dana Samuelson, president of American Gold Exchange.

He explained that gold and silver are, for most people, discretionary purchases - in other words, more of a want rather than a need. And when inflation erodes spending power, those discretionary purchases slow, Samuelson noted.

For now, it's tough to measure just how much the inflationary impulse of a roughly doubling of the diesel price in the last six months has had on the global economy, but the market could be starting to see the "first ripple of that inflationary impulse," he said.

"That may be what the declining silver price is telling us now, because silver's value is approximately 50% monetary and 50% commodity," said Samuelson. Gold has seen a smaller decline from record highs, but it's more of a precious metal - 90% monetary and 10% commodity, he said.

Silver is also more subject to investor sentiment than gold, said Robert Minter, director of ETF investment strategy at Aberdeen Investments.

Global central-bank purchases of gold were a key reason why prices for the metal reached a record high earlier this year, and central-bank purchases are a "strategic source" of demand for the yellow metal, said Minter. "That same-size strategic buyer does not exist for silver," he added, making it more sensitive to investor sentiment.

Silver's outsize selloff

It's true, however, that it's not unusual for silver prices to move a lot more than gold prices.

Silver's sharper price decline than gold reflects its "greater volatility, exposure to industrial demand, and the unwinding of earlier speculative enthusiasm," said Ryan McIntyre, president of Sprott.

Earlier this year, as prices for gold were on track to notch record highs, some traders looked for a cheaper and quicker way to participate in that rise, leading to what can be referred to as speculative enthusiasm in the market.

But volatility often accompanies large and quick moves, and that's particularly true when "turbulence hits major markets, causing liquidity-driven selloffs" like the one seen earlier this week, Samuelson said.

On Wednesday, silver for December delivery, the most active futures contract, fell 6.1%, the largest one-day drop since June 24, and settled at $55.88 an ounce, the lowest since Nov. 26, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Gold that day posted a modest decline of 1.7%.

Higher inflation readings are not surprising given high energy prices, but they still "spooked equity markets" Wednesday, said Samuelson. And when that happens, gold and silver prices can "temporarily suffer as a casualty of those selloffs," he said.

Once the dust settles from these market selloffs, gold and silver prices often rebound quickly due to bargain buying, Samuelson said.

Prices for both metals ended higher Thursday, even after producer-price index data also showed a bigger-than-expected rise. Silver rose slightly again on Friday, but was still down more than 6% on the week.

Looking further ahead, silver still has potential to find support from stronger demand, stemming from growth in artificial intelligence and the data-center build-out.

"Investment across smart-grid infrastructure and data transmission supports silver demand, and we see AI as a growth source for the next several years," said Trevor Yates, senior investment analyst at Global X ETFs. Silver's "increasing industrial utility" underpins the metal's growing physical scarcity, he noted, with the physical-market forecast to remain in deficit for the sixth straight year in 2026.

While silver could stay volatile in the short term, Yates said Global X ETFs increasingly sees precious metals as an "interesting opportunity" for 2027.

-Myra P. Saefong

data.title: Lithium Prices Analysis Retreat as Chinese Carbonate Falls From Its 2026 Peak
data.description:
Prices for lithium carbonate are moving in opposite directions from China, with prices pulling back from 2026 highs while lithium-related stock prices are struggling to hold onto their gains.

According to market data, lithium carbonate at press time was valued at CNY 104,400 per tonne, which is CNY 31,400, or 43.01%, higher over the last 12 months. However, the new reading is still below the highs seen in the market's big run-up this year.

Meanwhile, the stock-basket chart that accompanies this graph tells a similar tale of a slow and uneven recovery, but on a different measure of the market. It closed at 261.88, which was 0.96 points lower and 0.37% below for the day.

Chinese Lithium Carbonate Pulls Back From Its Peak

As illustrated in the Trading Economics chart, Chinese lithium carbonate prices have been trading at around CNY 72,000 per tonne since the end of 2025. The price increased steadily during the month of December before picking up the pace at the beginning of 2026.

The rally pushed the market above CNY 150,000 per tonne in January, after which there were a number of volatile moves over February and March. Source: Trading Economics

In particular, prices have remained on the rise since the spring and hit a high in May of almost CNY 200,000 per tonne. The market took a turn then. The prices fell through June and July and dipped slightly in August before dropping again in September and October.

Despite the 43.01% annual increase, the latest reading of CNY 104,400 positions carbonate at almost the same level as in late 2025. The pullback highlights the speed at which a powerful commodity rally can come to an end.

Lithium Stocks Struggle to Sustain Their Recovery

Meanwhile, the lithium-stock chart is alternating swings instead of a steady rise. The index has increased from approximately 120 in 2023 and dipped back into 2024 early this year.

The chart indicates that the support level is around 250-260, and the resistance level is around 290-300. These are levels of reference, but not price floors or ceilings. Source: TradingView

The rally started in late 2024, and the index crossed above 350, but a significant reversal in early 2025 reversed some of those gains.

Since then, the basket has fluctuated from about 250 to 350, dipped into the 220s in 2026, and resumed its upward trend toward 290. This was the lowest level since the 261.88 reading on January 1.

Technical Signals Point to Caution

Significantly, the technical chart is using a Bollinger Bands Strategy 20/2 period. The blue “BBandLE” markers mark long-entry signals, and the red “BBandSE” markers mark short-entry signals.

The most recent red marker is located close to a recent rebound high and then a pullback to 261.88. Nevertheless, such signals are not conclusive that the stock basket is going to keep on dropping.

For now, the two charts combined indicate gains over a longer timeframe have failed to offset what has been weak lately. Nevertheless, the market forces that impact lithium carbonate prices and those that impact a lithium-stock basket are not the same, and these should not be treated as synonyms.

data.title: Tesla’s ‘flying’ Roadster could reach India; bookings open from ₹5.01 lakh
data.description:
Tesla has opened Indian reservations for two configurations of its new Roadster electric sports car, while a third, potentially flight-capable version could reach selected buyers by invitation. The announcement comes as the American automaker’s registrations surged 836 per cent during April–September, placing it third in India’s luxury electric-vehicle market behind BMW and Mercedes-Benz.

Unlike its existing Model Y SUVs, the Roadster is a low-slung, two-seat sports car with removable roof panels, developed for extreme acceleration. Tesla says its design draws inspiration from the SR-71 and F-35 aircraft and incorporates SpaceX components.

Speed comes at a price

Indian customers can reserve Performance and Thrust configurations. Performance emphasises electric propulsion and aerodynamic grip, with a claimed zero-to-60 mph time below 1.6 seconds. Thrust adds rocket-inspired propulsion assistance, with a claimed time below 0.9 seconds. Production specifications remain subject to confirmation.

Both require an initial ₹5.01-lakh payment, according to reported Indian reservation details. Performance requires another ₹45.05 lakh within 10 days, taking the deposit to ₹50.06 lakh. Thrust requires another ₹2,45,24,000, bringing its deposit to ₹2,50,25,000. Final selling prices remain unannounced.

From rockets to roads

The third configuration, Rocket, could also make its debut in India, offering selected buyers the possibility of owning Tesla’s proposed flying sports car. Equipped with rocket-derived propulsion technology intended to enable flight, it would be available exclusively by invitation.

“It is definitely possible. It is just that it is by invitation,” an industry source familiar with developments told BusinessLine, referring to the prospect of Indian buyers accessing Rocket.

The source explained that automotive engineering has long borrowed technologies from aerospace, but rocket-derived propulsion could take that convergence further.

“It is a different dimension, where rocket technology comes inside the car, and it can fly,” the source said, describing the shift from conventional automotive propulsion towards technologies associated with space exploration.

The proposed flying capability remains subject to technical validation and regulatory approvals. Roadster production is targeted for 2028, initially with left-hand-drive vehicles. Indian deliveries have not been scheduled.

Tesla gains ground

Tesla registered 646 vehicles during April–September 2026, against 69 a year earlier, according to Vahan data compiled as of October 11. Its luxury EV market share rose to 14.6 per cent from 2.5 per cent. September registrations reached 296, overtaking Mercedes-Benz’s 128.

However, direct comparisons with established luxury manufacturers overlook differences in distribution reach and market maturity. Tesla has seven centres in India, while several established rivals operate networks exceeding 50 outlets, supported by longstanding customer relationships and repeat purchases.

Tesla’s direct-to-consumer model also requires greater customer awareness as the company expands beyond its initial markets.

The road beyond the hype

Tesla currently sells the five-seat Model Y from ₹50.89 lakh and six-seat Model Y L from ₹61.99 lakh. The latter targets Indian families seeking greater passenger and luggage space. Complimentary Acceleration Boost enables the Model Y L to reach 100 km/h in a claimed 4.5 seconds, with up to 681 km of WLTP range.

Tesla operates 20 Supercharger stalls across five stations and 28 Destination Charger stalls across seven stations. Three additional charging sites are planned by December.

The company intends to expand charging infrastructure across major cities and connecting highways, although it has not disclosed a numerical expansion target. Restrictions imposed by residential societies on home-charger installations remain another obstacle to wider adoption.

For Tesla, expanding its physical reach and overcoming charging barriers will determine whether early enthusiasm translates into sustained luxury EV sales..

data.title: Zelenskiy asked neighbours to let grain cargoes through, Hungary PM Magyar says
data.description:
Ukrainian President President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has asked neighbours Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Hungary to allow the transit of Ukrainian grain cargoes due to a Black Sea blockade, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Saturday.

Magyar, who agreed with Zelenskiy to reset Ukraine-Hungary ties at a bilateral meeting on Friday, said he would have no objections to the measure if the Ukrainian grain cargoes only passed through Hungary, private broadcaster RTL reported.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $82 Million As BlackRock Leads Friday’s Withdrawals
data.description:
TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $82.4 million in net outflows on October 16. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $71.8 million of withdrawals, with Fidelity’s FBTC recording about $10.6 million.

BlackRock’s flagship spot Bitcoin ETF accounted for most of the selling as US-listed Bitcoin investment funds closed Friday’s session with net withdrawals of approximately $82.4 million.

Farside Investors’ figures show that the iShares Bitcoin Trust, known as IBIT, lost $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund recorded around $10.6 million in net outflows, while the remaining products were broadly flat on the day.

That concentration matters because IBIT has become one of the clearest measures of Bitcoin demand through traditional brokerage accounts.

Another Uneven Week For ETF Demand

The latest withdrawals followed substantial redemptions earlier in the week. October 14 saw roughly $261 million leave the category, followed by a modest return to net inflows on October 15.

Friday’s negative session therefore suggests demand remains unsettled rather than following a clear trend.

Investors have seen considerably larger individual outflow days in the past. Earlier October withdrawals approached $485 million in a single session, demonstrating how rapidly demand through these products can shift.

Context Is Important

An ETF outflow is not a complete measure of institutional Bitcoin ownership, and it does not necessarily indicate that every underlying holder has abandoned a long-term position.

Net inflows into the US spot Bitcoin ETF market since the products launched remained substantial despite the latest withdrawals.

The next trading sessions will be important. A quick recovery would suggest another temporary adjustment, while continued redemptions from IBIT and FBTC would place greater emphasis on whether traditional investors are reducing their exposure amid broader market uncertainty.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: BEL Q2 results 2026 date out | Market sees up to 16% YoY revenue growth, defence order may drop - share outlook in focus
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The board of directors of Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) has scheduled its meeting on 30 October 2026 to consider and approve the September 2026 quarter results for the current financial year.

The defence stock announced this in an exchange filing on Friday. The market has estimated healthy Q2 results for the defence company in 2026. Various brokerages have predicted a double-digit revenue growth for the company, but its order flow is expected to drop YoY. Hence, the focus will be on the defence order that BEL received during the July to September 2026 quarter.

As mentioned above, the defence company informed the Indian exchanges about the board meeting date to announce Q2 Results 2026 through an exchange filing on Friday, saying, "We wish to inform that a meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company is scheduled to be held on Friday, 30th October, 2026 to consider and approve, inter alia, Unaudited Standalone & Consolidated Financial Results for the quarter ended 30th September, 2026."

The market is expecting a healthy report with a double-digit revenue growth for the BEL. According to Kotak Securities, BEL is expected to report Q2 revenue at Rs.6,720 crore, up 16% YoY. The brokerage has estimated the company's EBITDA at Rs.1,940 crore, with an EBITDA Margin of 28.90%. The Q2 profit growth is estimated 14.10% YoY at Rs.1,460 crore.

Another brokerage, Elara Securities, has predicted 12% YoY revenue growth for the July to September 2026 quarter, to Rs.6,487 crore. Elara's predicted EBITDA is Rs.1,778 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 27.40%. The brokerage has predicted Q2 net profit at Rs.1,778 crore.

Speaking on the BEL Q2 Results 2026, Mahesh M Ojha, VP - Research and Business Development at KC Securities, said, "Even though BEL is expected to report a healthy profit and revenue growth, its order book is expected to shrink YoY. Hence, the company's defence order during the second quarter of the current financial year will be under the radar of market observers, when BEL's Q2 Results 2026 are announced."

BEL share price finished around one percent lower at Rs.376.85 per share on the NSE. The defence stock has delivered zero returns YTD and has lost around 5% in 2026. BEL's share price has corrected by around 18% in six months and by 8% in one year.

Decoding the technical chart of BEL shares, Mahesh M Ojha of KC Securities said, "BEL share price is looking positive on the monthly chart. Rs.372-374 is acting as a good support zone for the defence stock. On breaking above Rs.388, we may see the BEL share price touch Rs.428 in the near term. So, existing investors may hold the scrip, maintaining a strict stop-loss at Rs.358. Fresh investors can also initiate buying with a strict stop-loss at Rs.358 for the upside target of Rs.428."

data.title: ECB may raise rates by 50 bps by mid-2027 as energy prices fuel inflation: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to raise interest rates by a cumulative 50 basis points by the first half of 2027 as elevated energy prices and persistent services inflation keep price pressures above target, according to a research report by ICICI Bank Global Markets.

The report said the ECB could deliver another 25 basis points rate hike before the end of 2026, followed by a further 25 basis points of tightening in the first half of 2027, assuming energy and commodity prices remain elevated.

Eurozone headline inflation, measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), accelerated to 3.8 per cent year-on-year in September from 3.2 per cent in August, driven largely by a sharp increase in energy prices.

Energy inflation rose to 18.9 per cent in September from 14.3 per cent in the previous month, while prices increased 4 per cent month-on-month, marking their fastest pace of growth in six months.

The report attributed the surge to geopolitical disruptions in West Asia, warning that oil and gas prices could remain elevated for longer amid continuing tensions.

Underlying price pressures also persisted, with core inflation rising marginally to 2.5 per cent in September from 2.4 per cent in August. Services inflation increased to 3.2 per cent from 3 per cent, indicating continued domestic price pressures that could slow the return of inflation to the ECB's 2 per cent target.

However, core goods inflation remained unchanged at 1.2 per cent, suggesting that the pass-through of higher energy costs into core goods prices had remained relatively contained so far.

The report said this trend offered some relief but warned that indirect effects from rising energy and transportation costs warranted monitoring.

Transport prices emerged as a major contributor to headline inflation, rising 9.8 per cent year-on-year in September compared with 7.8 per cent in August. Prices in the housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels category also accelerated to 5.3 per cent from 4.3 per cent.

Food inflation edged up to 1.1 per cent in September from 0.8 per cent in August, partly reflecting a sharp increase in vegetable prices.

ICICI Bank said the combination of elevated energy costs and sticky services inflation could complicate the ECB's efforts to bring inflation back to target, strengthening the case for further monetary tightening.

data.title: Marvell and Nvidia outlooks provide buying opportunities during downturn: GF
data.description:
The current downturn among semiconductor stocks has created a buying opportunity for quality names, such as Nvidia and Marvell , according to GF Securities.

GF analysts attended the OCP Global Summit in San Jose last week, which reflected a shift toward full-stack co-design across hyperscalers.

"Nvidia's networking roadmap now spans both co‑packaged optics and the new USFP pluggable standard, co‑developed with Cisco to raise density and serviceability inside AI factories," said GF analyst Jeff Pu in an investor report. "USFP modules deliver up to 12.8 Tb/s per module and 400 Gb/s per lane, achieving near‑CPO efficiency while retaining the flexibility of pluggables for field maintenance."

The USFP stands for ultra-dense small form factor pluggable and is a new optical transceiver standard used to connect massive AI data center clusters.

"Our U.S. tour to neoclouds suggests power availability and licensing remain decisive factors for expansion," Pu noted. "However, there is no power shortage issue by now and in the foreseeable future, as most sites located far from urban centers, and many use stable gas‑based generation. For electricity cost, regional cost spreads remain wide, driving migration of new builds toward the southern corridor and select overseas zones such as Italy. For shell, the modular datacenter shells can be completed in as little as three months, but liquid‑cooling infrastructure continues to be the bottleneck."

The tour also revealed the rising importance of CPU for inference, especially for agentic AI. This is expected to double the total addressable market for CPUs.

"GPU utilization for decode workloads averages only 20–30%, and SRAM‑based accelerators struggle with long‑context efficiency," Pu said. "Token costs are falling 5–10× every year, but semi and memory costs are rising. Bottlenecks are NAND, DRAM, and cooling. The agentic AI factory model—where orchestration and retrieval run on CPUs—reshapes unit economics: CPU‑to‑accelerator ratios move from 1:4–1:8 in chat‑era systems to 1:1 in agentic deployments."

"Despite the broad market softness, we suggest investors accumulate quality stocks," he added. "We continue to like Nvidia, PTFE sector, MRVL (DSP, Google attach, Maia 300), and the CPU supply chain ."

However, risks include AI demand slowdown, infrastructure deployment, supply constraints and competition.

data.title: AI rapidly improving, could vastly boost US GDP, Anthropic's Clark tells policymakers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Internal model forecasts US GDP could reach $44 trillion by 2030 under certain conditions
  • Clark says window to impose AI safeguards is shrinking
  • Clark urged international cooperation on regulation

By David Lawder

Rapidly improving artificial intelligence capabilities will bring far faster change across all fields, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday, with one of the company's internal models forecasting that under certain conditions it could increase US economic output by almost 50% by 2030.

Clark, speaking at IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said that international cooperation was needed to erect "unusual and serious rules" for the transformative technology, and there was a shrinking window for policymakers to act.

Clark said that the estimated potential US GDP of $44 trillion, which compares to the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery.

He said the forecast assumed "the technology continuing to get better. And if GDP were to grow this much, then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need to have been created to power such a major economic expansion".

Clark's remarks come as the company prepares for an initial public offering expected in November that could value the firm at up to $2 trillion.

HUMANS IN CONTROL, FOR NOW

Clark issued a wake-up call to policymakers about the speed of AI development, saying there was growing evidence of a "singularity" where AI development outpaces human control.

"We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially great peril," he said in a lecture to hundreds of government and finance officials.

AI was a major topic at the IMF and World Bank meetings, as both a source of growth offsetting high energy prices and a potential threat to stability if it falls short of its promise as a productivity game-changer and stock valuations crash.

Officials also expressed worries about AI destroying certain jobs and leaving some countries behind.

But Clark, a former journalist who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit," painted a picture of a rosy future where AI was a force multiplier for scientific discovery, solving mathematical, engineering and biological problems, including new drug discovery, as human researchers are supplemented by hundreds or thousands of AI assistants.

More countries can participate in the AI revolution by helping to build the data center computing capacity needed to power AI, he said.

STRICTEST CONTROLS ON BIOLOGICAL RESEARCH

Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology.

"Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have many choices to make," he said.

Biological research, where AI has already created new viruses, is an area "where we want the strictest human oversight and transparency to maintain safety."

Despite some recent high-profile incidents where rogue AI systems have escaped testing environments and hacked websites and databases, he said AI was still under human control. But the window to impose safeguards was shrinking as AI became more capable and was now "a small number of years."

Clark also acknowledged that AI was causing job losses in some fields with "high AI exposure" such as call centers and customer service personnel. But for other fields, such as scientific research, he said AI was enhancing employment and a major unknown was its potential to create jobs in completely new industries.

data.title: It was another great week for the average stock as market leadership shifts away from tech
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis and Isabel Wang

The S&P 500's tech sector just had its worst week in a year and a half, while an equal-weighted version of the index cemented a second-straight weekly advance

The average stock in the S&P 500 just had a decent week, although a slump in tech masked that shine at the index level.

Investors aren't bailing on the stock market, despite an ugly selloff in technology names this week that helped to saddle the S&P 500 with its worst weekly showing in months.

The S&P 500 SPX lost almost 2% even as the majority of the index's stocks actually advanced on the week. Seventy percent of stocks in the index posted weekly gains while 30% fell, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That helped the equal-weighted version of the index XX:SP500EW cement a second-straight week in the green. When the dust had settled, the S&P 500 had cemented its worst weekly showing since June, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Following a powerful but narrow tech-led rally, this week's action offered the latest indication that market leadership is shifting once again. While tech stocks and some industrial names tied to the artificial-intelligence build-out slumped this week, the average stock in the increasingly top-heavy S&P 500 made it through a difficult week largely unscathed.

Defensive and interest-rate-sensitive areas of the market moved sharply higher this week, as stocks that had lagged over the past two months shot upward. This has given hard-hit corners of the market a chance to shine.

"Given that there's growing concerns around the AI trade and volatility in spending these companies are doing, it just makes sense for investors to broaden their view a little bit and look for other opportunities," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial, in a phone interview Friday. "Now money is rotating out of tech into areas that had been really depressed."

Certainly, it helped that interest rates in the bond market saw a big pullback from recent highs, providing some broad relief to stocks.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, a popular exchange-traded fund that equally weights stocks in the index, rose 0.5% this week. By contrast, the S&P 500 saw its biggest weekly percentage drop since June 26.

The big drag on the S&P 500 is its largest sector, information technology XX:SP500.45, which was pummeled this week with a 6.4% drop. That left the tech sector with its biggest weekly loss since April 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Meanwhile, seven of the S&P 500's 11 sectors saw weekly gains, FactSet data showed.

"Nobody really wants to be out of the market," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, in a phone interview Friday. "If people were really genuinely concerned about the stock market right now, they'd be selling and not rushing to buy something else."

Among traditionally defensive areas of the stock market, the S&P 500's consumer-staples sector XX:SP500.30 surged 5% this week. Another defensive area, healthcare XX:SP500.35, had a big climb of 3.4%, while rate-sensitive stocks like materials XX:SP500.15 and utilities XX:SP500.55 also jumped sharply.

The decline in interest rates this week was significant, as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y "backed off pretty dramatically," Saglimbene noted. The 10-year Treasury rate fell this week to 5.097% on Friday, locking in its biggest weekly pullback since February, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Bond yields move inversely with bond prices.

That's down from the 10-year rate's recent high of 5.31% on Oct. 5. Yields on 10-year and 30-year BX:TMUBMUSD30Y Treasurys have risen to their highest levels in decades this year.

"With some improvement on the rates front, people do feel it's safe to move some money back into rate-sensitive sectors like financials XX:SP500.40, industrials XX:SP500.20 and real estate XX:SP500.60," Sosnick said.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury dropped Thursday despite a hot reading on wholesale inflation from the producer-price index that same day, partly because "there was a bit of a flight-to-safety trade on top of it surrounding CoreWeave," Sosnick said - referring to the neocloud company (CRWV) whose stock tumbled this week on worries over its AI-related borrowing.

Tech had been the stock market's "safety trade," rising when Treasury yields were spiking in September, as investors appeared confident about the AI trade continuing to power higher despite higher rates, said Keith Lerner, CIO at Truist Wealth, by phone on Friday.

Last month, tech looked like "the only place in town," he noted, "while all these other areas were beat up." Now, it appears the tide has turned.

"Instead of a broad-based selloff across the board, you're just seeing a rotation from tech to everything else," Lerner said. "A rotational market is better than when money is broadly leaving the market."

data.title: Hari, shankar, mahadev: the enigma behind skyexchange
data.description:
Syndicate Kingpin Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal (HST) owner of Skyexchange. ED says HST’s SkyExchange and the Mahadev App were run in Partnership, “A constituent part of the same criminal enterprise."

HST Wins Curbs On The Press In Delhi's Lower Courts

But ED’s Raipur Files Tell Another Story

He carries two Gods in his name. Hari is Vishnu, the preserver. Shankar is Shiva, whom devotees also call Mahadev.

In the files of India's Enforcement Directorate (ED), the aganecy probing money laundering, the third name follows close behind.

The ED says Hari Shankar Tibrewal’s betting platform, SkyExchange, was “co-owned and co-promoted in partnership with” the promoters of Mahadev Online Book. That made it, in the agency’s words, “a constituent part of the same criminal enterprise.” Mahadev is the app at the centre of one of India’s largest betting investigations, which the ED estimates generated Rs 75,000–80,000 crore.

To the men around him, he was simply “Hari Bhai.” In an astrologer’s WhatsApp chat recovered from a jailed businessman’s phone, he appears only as three letters and a date of birth: “HST.” In the ED’s charge sheet he is Accused No. 24. The ED twice summoned him to Raipur, and twice the record reads: “Did not appear.”

And in a Delhi courtroom on September 23, he won a court order restricting what the press may call him.

THE ENIGMA

Delhi courts have restrained some news outlets from branding him with labels. But EDs own documents, which no injunction covers, describe in detail the man they call “HST”

A judge confirmed interim injunctions in HST's civil defamation suit. The judge found that publications calling him a “Hawala Trader”, a “key figure in stock market manipulation scheme” and a “shadowy titan in a financial underworld” prima facie attributed criminality to a man no court has convicted. The court also found that later articles using words such as “absconding”, “farar” and “fugitive from Indian justice” fell within the category of material it had already ordered taken down.

To Tibrewal, it was vindication. To a growing number of newsrooms, it has become something else: a legal tool that hangs over any outlet trying to write about him.

“Those accused of white-collar crimes are using the law to gag the media. It gives them a cover, and it intimidates the very press that can put pressure on the system protecting them,” a lawyer of a leading Delhi news agency told BW.

In case of HST, the order does not stop the story being told. The court did not impose a blanket ban on reporting about Tibrewal. As reported, it distinguished between branding a man a criminal and fairly reporting what investigators and courts have said, and it left the second untouched. That matters, because the investigators have said a great deal.

THE MAN IN THE FILES

The ED has filed two documents this year in the Mahadev betting-app case. The first is Provisional Attachment Order No. 16/2026 of June 5. The second is a 375-page supplementary prosecution complaint filed in Raipur in September. Neither treats Tibrewal as a peripheral figure.

The attachment order calls him “HST.”

It says the betting platform SkyExchange was “operated by Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal from Kolkata” and was “co-owned and co-promoted in partnership with” Mahadev’s promoters Sourabh Chandrakar and Ravi Uppal, making it “a constituent part of the same criminal enterprise.” The ED’s first hook on him was a 2020 FIR at Kolkata’s Burtolla police station.

The charge sheet names him Accused No. 24 and describes him as a man who “hails from Kolkata but currently residing in Dubai.”

In its section on EaseMyTrip co-founder Nishant Pitti, it uses a phrase no Delhi court has struck from an ED filing: “Syndicate Kingpin Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal (owner of Skyexchange).”

SUMMONED TWICE, APPEARED NEVER

Both documents record the same thing. The ED summoned Tibrewal under Section 50 of the PMLA on April 22, 2024 and again on April 25, 2024. Both times the entry reads: “Did not appear.”

He has not appeared since, according to the documents. Since then the agency has frozen Rs 580.78 crore of securities it says he beneficially owns, named him as an accused, attached Rs 940 crore of assets linked to an alleged business partner, and filed a sixth supplementary charge sheet with his name on almost every page that matters. He is now understood to be in London, sources say.

Rs 22 CR A Week

The ED’s estimate of the SkyExchange business is built on one ledger, seized from Prashant Bagri, who the charge sheet says has been “an employee of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal since 2017.” The ledger listed the platform’s super-admins and a single week’s earnings: about Rs 22 crore. Extrapolated from 2016, the ED puts SkyExchange’s proceeds at Rs 11,000–12,000 crore, alongside an estimated Rs 75,000–80,000 crore for Mahadev.

It says Mahadev’s promoters held admin IDs on SkyExchange and could create “master and Super IDs.” In the ED’s words, they were partners running “both the said Applications parallelly with same modus-operandi.”

The world around that money is described in the same charge sheet: - A Rs 200-crore wedding for Chandrakar in Ras Al Khaimah, paid in cash. - Private jets from Nagpur, and Rs 112 crore sent by hawala to an event company. - Call centres run out of villas in Dubai’s Al Barsha district, each housing 50 to 70 people.

THE 30% CASHBACK

The most damaging passages describe how, according to the ED, betting money became stock-market money.

Tibrewal, the charge sheet says, “invests huge amount of funds in Indian Listed entities after making the deals with the Promoters of the said Indian entities and in return, the Indian entities have to pay cashback (in the range of 30% to 40% of total investment) in cash.” The cash was collected in Delhi, it says, by his associate Gagan Gupta (“Gagan Bhai”) and Gupta’s men.

ED Names the Deals: -

Salasar Techno Engineering. Investments of Rs 81.9 crore in 2022 and about Rs 130 crore in 2024. The ED says the promoters returned about Rs 25 crore and Rs 40 crore in cash “in cash and Hawala Channels.” - Tiger Logistics. A fixer told the ED he collected Rs 5–6 crore in cash from the promoter as “cashback (30% of total investment)” and handed it to Gupta’s associates.

EaseMyTrip. Tibrewal’s front fund, AG Dynamic Funds, allegedly bought 1.51 crore shares worth Rs 59.6 crore after a “pre-arranged” deal with Pitti. Pitti has called the allegations “completely baseless.” -

Toyam Sports. A seized tracking sheet lists shareholdings against the name “Hari.” - Vikas Garg’s companies. Rs 765.77 crore allegedly went into the companies of Garg, the Delhi businessman, which used it to buy the US software firm Ebix.

A WARDROBE OF FUNDS

Instead of simply hoarding illegal cash, Tibrewal structured a system to inject betting proceeds into the Indian equity market using the Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) route. This route was actively leveraged to corner stakes in small, mid-cap, and SME-listed companies.

The ED attributes a long list of offshore vehicles to him: - Funds: AG Dynamic Funds, Forbes EMF, Coeus Global, Ebisu Global, Oyster Bay, Plutus, and Tano Investment Opportunities in Mauritius. - Dubai companies: Zenith Multi Trading DMCC, Plus Commodities, Ecotek General Trading, Caterfiled Global and JE Impex.

The ED Also Details the Disguises:

Ecotek. A witness told the ED that the recorded 100% owner was “just benamidar of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal.”

Zenith. The registered email address, the ED says, belongs to Tibrewal. - Tano. The attachment order says he “changed the beneficial ownership… mid-investigation, immediately upon issuance of summons.”

When the ED asked Tano to identify its owner, it named four entities, all of which ignored summons. Then Mauritius’s Financial Services Commission wrote to SEBI identifying Tibrewal as the beneficial owner. The ED notes the letter came “post every attempt… to show that Hari Shankar Tibrewal is not the beneficial owner.”

“HARI BHAI” AT THE TAJ

The charge sheet also places HST at the centre of the Ebix takeover. According to two witnesses, Tibrewal was at meetings at the Taj hotel in London in mid-2024 with Vikas Garg. Shown his photograph, he was identified as “the main investor on behalf of all the entities.” Travel records, the ED says, back their accounts.

Sunil Bhandari, another accused, told investigators that Garg and Tibrewal “are partners and involved in price rigging of certain listed entities by using the funds generated at Skyexchange.”

Garg, now the only one of 14 arrested accused still in custody, at first told the ED he knew Tibrewal was in illegal betting. After his arrest he said he did not know him. The ED says Garg’s seized iPhone holds a February 2025 call in which he discusses money with Gagan Gupta and refers to “Hari, Hari Bhai.” It also holds a WhatsApp exchange with an astrologer about “HST,” giving a date of birth the ED says matches Tibrewal’s.

The KOLKATA NETWORK

Before Dubai, there was Kolkata.

The ED's attachment order says SkyExchange was "operated by Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal from Kolkata." The trail starts in the city too. The first case linked to him was an FIR registered on 24 September 2020 at Burtolla police station, in the heart of north Kolkata's old trading district. Kolkata Police filed a charge sheet in that case on 29 October 2024 under the IPC and the West Bengal Gambling and Prize Competitions Act. (Charge sheet, Burtolla FIR details; attachment order.)

The ED says the money ran through the city's shell-company economy:

Cash into bank entries. Kolkata entry operator Amit Saraogi (A-37) told the ED he provided "bank entries to the tune of Rs. 150 crore against cash" to Ability Games Ltd, Swamim Vanijya and Nischaya Trading. The charge sheet describes those as companies "of Mr Hari Shankar Tibrewal." He said he did this on the instructions of Sanjeev Bera, whom the ED describes as Tibrewal's employee. (Chargesheet, Saraogi statement.)

Another Rs 200 crore in entries went to companies of Suraj Chokhani (A-25), whom the ED describes as the man who "manages the operations of Indian entities of Mr. Hari Shankar Tibrewal." (Charge sheet, Saraogi statement; Gagan Gupta call records.)

The shell factory. Saraogi's companies used dummy directors. Reports of his statement say he ran 40–50 shells, paid the dummy directors Rs 1,500–3,000 a month, and earned 1.25% commission. (Charge sheet; edatabook, May 2024.)

The phone records. Call records of Gagan Gupta show him in "regular touch" with Tibrewal, Saraogi, Chokhani and Bagri. The ED calls this the inner circle around SkyExchange. (Chargesheet.)

The pipeline. Again and again, the charge sheet says money that reached Vikas Garg's companies and Sunil Bhandari's firms came originally "from Kolkata based shell entities," arranged by Tibrewal.

A casino deal. Ability Games Ltd (A-26), which the charge sheet lists among Tibrewal's companies, signed an agreement to buy the Nepal casino business of the listed gaming company Delta Corp, according to reports of the ED's findings. (edatabook/Free Press Journal; check against Delta Corp's stock-exchange filing before use.)

THE QUESTIONS INDIA HASN'T ANSWERED

The ED says Tibrewal has twice declined to appear before it. It calls him the owner of a Rs 11,000-crore betting platform and lists him as an accused in a money-laundering prosecution. That raises questions the agency has not publicly answered.

Fugitive Economic Offenders Act. The 2018 Act lets the ED ask a special court to declare someone a fugitive economic offender if a warrant has been issued, the offence exceeds Rs 100 crore, and the person has left India and refuses to return. Has the ED moved such an application against Tibrewal?

Warrant. Is there a non-bailable warrant against him? The new charge sheet seeks warrants against Gagan Gupta and two others, but does not list Tibrewal among them. Why?

Extradition. India has an extradition treaty with the UAE, and has used it in other cases. Has India sought his extradition, or a Red Notice? Ministry of External Affairs and ED must look

If he is in the UK, India–UK extradition proceedings are slow; see the Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya cases. Is this the reason that those wanted in cases like HST shift to London?

Until those questions are answered, the record shows a contrast. The man the ED calls a “Syndicate Kingpin” has not answered its summons in Raipur, while in Delhi he has won injunctions against outlets that wrote about him.

An “Escapee” from India who's yet to be delcared an Absconder. Delhi's lower court's need to take the ED cases and summons into account.

Tibrewal has denied any role in the Mahadev app or SkyExchange and rejects the allegations against him. None of the charges has been tested at trial. But he remains outside India and does not appear before ED.

Palak Shah

BW Reporters Palak Shah is a seasoned investigative journalist and the fearless author of The Market Mafia: Chronicle of India’s High-Tech Stock Market Scandal & The Cabal That Went Scot-Free, a hard-hitting exposé that unmasked the shadowy underbelly of India’s financial markets. With nearly two decades of boots-on-the-ground reporting in Mumbai, Palak has carved a reputation as a relentless truth-seeker, diving deep into the nexus of money, power, and regulation. His bylines have graced India’s most prestigious financial dailies, including The Economic Times, Business Standard, The Financial Express, and The Hindu Business Line, where his incisive coverage has shaped narratives and rattled boardrooms. Drawn to crime reporting at the tender age of 19, Palak quickly realized that Mumbai’s gritty gang wars of the 1980s had given way to a slicker, more insidious form of organized crime—white-collar schemes orchestrated in corporate towers. This epiphany fueled his pivot to financial journalism, where he’s spent years decoding the complex machinations of India’s ‘white money’ economy. From stock market manipulations to regulatory loopholes, Palak’s work peels back the polished veneer of high finance to reveal the cabals pulling the strings. His passion for uncovering truth, backed by a knack for connecting dots others miss, makes him a formidable voice in Indian journalism, unafraid to challenge the status quo and expose the players who think they’re untouchable.

data.title: IDBI Bank Sale: Government Says Employee Concerns Addressed
data.description:
The Finance Ministry says existing employees’ service conditions and pension benefits will be protected under the proposed Rs 52,878 crore stake sale

The government has said legitimate concerns of IDBI Bank employees and other stakeholders have been addressed through provisions in the share purchase agreement for the lender’s proposed privatisation, even as employee associations continue to oppose the transaction.

Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary told the Lok Sabha that safeguards for existing employees and other stakeholders had been incorporated into the agreement. The response came amid questions about the potential impact of the proposed sale on employees and whether the government had consulted bank staff and their representatives.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to 10955230 Canada Inc., a subsidiary of Fairfax Financial Holdings, for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction involves the government selling its 30.48 per cent holding and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) divesting its 30.24 per cent stake. Following the sale, the government will retain 15 per cent and LIC 19 per cent.

The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has separately stated that existing employees’ service conditions will remain protected and pension benefits will be safeguarded through a dedicated pension fund.

However, the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees has disputed claims that employee representatives were consulted during the process. The forum has called for the transaction to be reviewed, citing concerns over employee safeguards, the bank’s valuation and the implications of transferring control to a foreign investor. It has also sought greater transparency over the valuation methodology and transaction terms.

The proposed disinvestment process began with the publication of a preliminary information memorandum on 7 October 2022, inviting expressions of interest from potential bidders. The transaction remains subject to the required regulatory approvals and completion procedures.

The competing positions highlight the importance of employee protections and consultation as the government advances the strategic sale of the bank.

data.title: India Excludes Sugar-Based Ethanol From 2026-27 Tender
data.description:
State-run oil marketing companies seek 11 billion litres of ethanol from grain-based feedstocks, while reducing the price incentive for corn-based supplies

India has set sugar diversion for ethanol production at zero for the 2026-27 supply year, excluding sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from the latest procurement tender. The move comes amid concerns over domestic sugar availability, lower production prospects and rising prices.

The tender, issued on 16 October by Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, invites bids for 11 billion litres of ethanol for the supply year beginning in November. Suppliers can offer ethanol made from corn, broken rice and surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India.

The decision signals a shift in feedstock procurement as India seeks to balance its ethanol-blending programme with the need to maintain domestic sugar supplies.

Grain-Based Ethanol Takes Priority

The tender states that the government has directed oil marketing companies to reduce sugar diversion for ethanol production to zero for the 2026-27 supply year. Accordingly, the companies have not invited bids for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses.

India has used surplus sugar and sugarcane-based feedstocks to support ethanol production and reduce dependence on imported crude oil. The latest tender instead directs procurement towards grain-based alternatives, including corn and rice.

The change comes as poor rainfall in key sugar-producing states, including Maharashtra and Karnataka, has raised concerns about sugar output. Lower production prospects have added pressure to domestic supplies and prices.

Corn Ethanol Incentive Falls

The tender also reduces the incentive for corn-based ethanol to Rs 2.79 per litre from Rs 5.79 per litre. The procurement price consequently falls to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86 per litre.

The lower incentive changes the commercial terms for suppliers that use corn as a feedstock. The impact on procurement and production will depend on the economics of grain availability, processing costs and the prices offered under the tender.

The procurement framework allows suppliers to use surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India, alongside corn and broken rice. This provides alternative feedstocks as sugar-based ethanol remains outside the latest tender.

India has expanded ethanol blending to reduce crude oil imports and curb pollution. The government made the E20 blend, which contains 20 per cent ethanol, the nationwide mandatory standard earlier in 2026. However, some motorists have raised concerns about its compatibility with older vehicles.

data.title: HDFC Bank Q2 Profit Rises 5%, Misses Estimates At Rs 19,510 Cr
data.description:
India’s largest private-sector lender reports a year-on-year increase in second-quarter profit, while net interest income falls short of forecasts and provisions rise amid improving asset quality

HDFC Bank reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of the 2026–27 financial year, but the result fell short of market expectations.

The lender’s net profit was below the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 19,727 crore. It had reported a profit of Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.

The results, announced on Saturday, 17 October, reflect continued growth in the bank’s core lending business, alongside higher provisioning expenses and weaker-than-expected operating performance.

Net Interest Income Misses Forecast

Net interest income (NII), which measures the difference between interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits, rose 10 per cent year-on-year to Rs 34,619 crore.

However, the figure was below the estimated Rs 34,991 crore.

Operating profit increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,483 crore, compared with Rs 27,923 crore in the year-ago period. The result also missed the market estimate of Rs 29,868 crore.

The bank’s net interest margin (NIM), based on total assets, stood at 3.16 per cent.

Provisions Increase, Asset Quality Improves

HDFC Bank’s provisions rose to Rs 3,574 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 3,059 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs 3,500 crore a year earlier.

Despite the increase in provisions, asset quality improved sequentially.

The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio declined to 1.11 per cent from 1.17 per cent in the previous quarter, beating the estimated 1.14 per cent. The net NPA ratio also fell to 0.37 per cent from 0.41 per cent, against an estimate of 0.39 per cent.

The improvement in these ratios indicates a lower proportion of stressed loans relative to the bank’s advances, although provisioning costs remain an important factor for earnings.

Loan Growth Remains Strong

HDFC Bank continued to expand its lending portfolio during the quarter.

Average advances under management increased 14.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.87 lakh crore. Gross advances at the end of September stood at Rs 32.20 lakh crore, representing growth of 16.3 per cent from a year earlier.

Retail loans grew 11.7 per cent year-on-year, while lending to small and mid-market enterprises increased 23.5 per cent.

On the funding side, average deposits rose 16.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.66 lakh crore. Average current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 10.7 per cent to Rs 9.71 lakh crore.

The results highlight the bank’s continued loan and deposit growth, even as its profitability metrics remain below market expectations in some key areas.
